beats.label: S1 · McNulty breaks rank
beats.text: After Stringer Bell intimidates a witness into acquitting D'Angelo, detective Jimmy McNulty tells a judge that BPD ignores the Barksdale drug empire, forcing brass to build a detail.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The out-of-turn complaint is the inciting act that creates the detail and defines McNulty's insubordinate relationship with command going forward.

beats.label: S1 · The detail takes shape
beats.text: Lieutenant Cedric Daniels is told to run a passive investigation, but Lester Freamon and Prez turn the dumping-ground unit into real police, building toward a wiretap on the Barksdale pagers.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes Daniels, Freamon, Prez and the wiretap methodology that defines how this show does police work from here on.

beats.label: S1 · D'Angelo runs the Pit
beats.text: Demoted to the low-rises, D'Angelo Barksdale reluctantly manages young dealers Bodie, Poot and Wallace while his uncle Avon and Stringer keep the real operation insulated above him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Positions D'Angelo as the soft point in the organisation and introduces the Pit crew whose fates drive the season's moral spine.

beats.label: S1 · Omar's war with Avon
beats.text: Stickup man Omar Little robs a Barksdale stash, so Avon has Omar's boyfriend Brandon tortured and killed; Omar retaliates by shooting enforcer Stinkum and agreeing to testify for McNulty.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The Omar-Barksdale blood feud is the season's engine and establishes Omar as a permanent wildcard against the organisation.

beats.label: S1 · Wallace can't take it
beats.text: Haunted by finding Brandon's body, Wallace goes home to his grandmother; when he drifts back to Baltimore, Stringer orders his death and Bodie and Poot pull the trigger on their friend.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Wallace's murder is the moral hinge that breaks D'Angelo and reframes Stringer and Bodie in every later season.

beats.label: S1 · Politics kills the case
beats.text: When the detail traces drug money to senator Clay Davis, the investigation is throttled from above; the FBI would rather chase the Barksdales' political corruption than help make street cases.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets the show's core thesis — institutions protect themselves — and plants Clay Davis and the political layer for later seasons.

beats.label: S1 · Everyone gets punished
beats.text: Avon takes a short sentence and Wee-Bey eats the murders, leaving Stringer running the business; D'Angelo learns Wallace is dead but stays quiet after his mother visits, while McNulty is exiled to the marine unit.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets the exact board for season 2: Avon inside, Stringer in charge, D'Angelo bitter but silent, McNulty banished — every launching condition sits here.

cliffhanger.text: The Barksdales took a plea and the detail is dissolved. Avon and D'Angelo are in prison, Stringer is running the business from a funeral home, and McNulty has been buried on a police boat for embarrassing the brass.
questions: Can Stringer actually run the operation without Avon on the street?
Will D'Angelo stay loyal now that he knows Wallace was murdered on Stringer's order?
Does McNulty ever get back to real police work, or does the department bury him for good?

characters.name: Jimmy McNulty
characters.line: Homicide detective whose complaint started the case; punished for it by reassignment to the marine unit.

characters.name: Stringer Bell
characters.line: Avon's underboss and business mind, now running the Barksdale organisation alone from a funeral home front while studying economics at community college.

characters.name: Avon Barksdale
characters.line: West Baltimore drug kingpin, imprisoned on a short sentence after pleading out; still expects the empire to be his when he returns.

characters.name: D'Angelo Barksdale
characters.line: Avon's nephew, imprisoned for a much longer stretch; knows Stringer had Wallace killed but stayed quiet after his mother Brianna talked him down.

characters.name: Cedric Daniels
characters.line: Lieutenant who ran the detail; passed over for promotion after refusing to shut the case down, with a suspicious FBI file hanging over him.

characters.name: Lester Freamon
characters.line: Quiet detail veteran revealed as the sharpest investigator in the room; promoted into homicide as the case ends.

characters.name: Kima Greggs
characters.line: Narcotics detective shot in the ambush that killed Orlando; survived, back on her feet, romantically partnered off the job.

characters.name: Omar Little
characters.line: Shotgun-carrying stickup man at war with the Barksdales; lost his boyfriend Brandon and killed Stinkum in return, now robbing dealers in New York.

characters.name: Bodie Broadus
characters.line: Pit corner kid promoted up the ranks; shot Wallace on Stringer's order and carries it.

characters.name: Wee-Bey Brice
characters.line: Barksdale enforcer and the organisation's designated fall guy, confessing to a stack of murders including ones he did not commit.

beats.label: S2 · Empire in trouble
beats.text: Stringer runs the corners while Avon serves out his sentence. Avon burns a supplier for a shorter bid, and New York cuts the Barksdales off.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets the supply crisis that pushes Stringer to Joe, which triggers everything else this season.

beats.label: S2 · The Greek's docks
beats.text: Union chief Frank Sobotka smuggles containers for a crime boss called the Greek to save his dying docks. A container arrives full of dead women.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the parallel plot and the killing that becomes the season's investigative hook.

beats.label: S2 · A grudge detail
beats.text: Valchek's petty feud with Sobotka wins Daniels a detail. It stumbles onto the smuggling and realises Sobotka's docks are the Greek's pipeline.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains why the detail exists and why it ends up pointed at the Greek instead of a street case.

beats.label: S2 · Stringer moves
beats.text: Desperate for product, Stringer cuts a deal with Joe for his supply. Fearing D'Angelo will snitch from prison, he has him murdered and staged as suicide.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Two Stringer power plays that fracture the Barksdale family and reshape who supplies Baltimore.

beats.label: S2 · Avon strikes back
beats.text: Avon, furious Stringer sold his territory to Joe, hires New York enforcer Brother Mouzone. Stringer tricks Omar into shooting Mouzone with a lie about Brandon.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Opens the Avon/Stringer rift and creates two enemies who now know Stringer plays dirty.

beats.label: S2 · Sobotka silenced
beats.text: The detail traces the smuggling to the Greek and arrests Sobotka. He agrees to flip, but a bent FBI agent tips the Greeks off and Sobotka is murdered.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains why the docks storyline ends without prosecution and how the Greek walks away clean.

beats.label: S2 · New pipeline
beats.text: Nick informs, but the Greek and Vondas have already fled the country. Joe takes over their pipeline, and the detail pivots to hunt him and Stringer.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets the S3-forward state: Joe is now the supply, Stringer is the new target.

cliffhanger.text: Stringer and Joe now share Baltimore's drug supply, with the Greek's operation quietly folded into theirs. The detail is coming for both, and Avon is still watching from prison.
questions: How will Avon respond from prison to the alliance Stringer built without him?
Now that Omar and Mouzone both know Stringer set them up, who moves first?
Can the detail bring Stringer and Joe down without Sobotka's testimony to lean on?

characters.name: Stringer Bell
characters.line: Runs the Barksdales while Avon is inside; cut a supply deal with Joe against Avon's orders, had D'Angelo killed, and set Omar on Mouzone.

characters.name: Avon Barksdale
characters.line: Still in prison, furious Stringer sold territory to Joe behind his back and hired Brother Mouzone to defend the corners.

characters.name: Jimmy McNulty
characters.line: Detective who forced the harbor case back to Baltimore and joined the detail chasing the drug trade at the top.

characters.name: Cedric Daniels
characters.line: Runs the new detail; scrapped his plan to leave the force and is now aimed at Stringer and Joe.

characters.name: Proposition Joe
characters.line: East side kingpin who has taken over the Greek's Baltimore supply and is now Stringer's partner.

characters.name: Omar Little
characters.line: Freelance stick-up artist; shot Mouzone after Stringer's lie about Brandon, then realised he had been played.

characters.name: Brother Mouzone
characters.line: New York enforcer hired by Avon to hold the corners; survived Omar's ambush and knows Stringer set him up.

characters.name: Frank Sobotka
characters.line: Stevedore union chief who smuggled for the Greek to fund the docks; killed by the Greeks before he could testify.

characters.name: The Greek
characters.line: Baltimore's shadow smuggling boss; fled overseas with his lieutenant Vondas after a bent FBI contact tipped him off.

beats.label: S3 · Corners Razed
beats.text: With Barksdale corners razed by the city, Stringer forms a dealer co-op to share supply. Young rival Marlo Stanfield refuses to join and starts taking corners.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the Marlo threat and Stringer's business-first pivot that will drive the whole season.

beats.label: S3 · Hamsterdam
beats.text: Sick of the drug war, Major Colvin quietly designates three abandoned blocks where dealers can sell without arrest. Crime in his district plummets.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's central experiment; its collapse is the political event that reshapes the department and Carcetti's opening.

beats.label: S3 · Avon Returns
beats.text: Avon Barksdale is paroled and demands war on Marlo, while Stringer wants to abandon the corners for real estate. Their partnership fractures.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The schism at the top of the Barksdale organization sets up the mutual betrayal that ends it.

beats.label: S3 · D'Angelo's Death
beats.text: McNulty proves D'Angelo's jailhouse death was murder and confronts Brianna. Cornered by Avon, Stringer admits he ordered the hit to protect the family.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The confession is the point of no return between the two men; every later betrayal traces to this moment.

beats.label: S3 · Mutual Betrayal
beats.text: They sell each other out. Stringer hands Avon's address to Colvin; Avon feeds Stringer's location to Omar and Brother Mouzone.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The mechanism that removes both Barksdales from the board in a single stroke, leaving Marlo unopposed.

beats.label: S3 · Stringer's End
beats.text: Omar and Mouzone corner Stringer in a half-built development and shoot him dead. McNulty arrests Avon the next day; Marlo watches from a distance.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The vacuum Marlo will fill in season 4 is created here. Both faces of the old regime are gone.

beats.label: S3 · Hamsterdam Falls
beats.text: The press exposes Hamsterdam. Rawls raids it, Colvin is forced out, and Carcetti uses the scandal to launch his mayoral campaign.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ends Colvin's police career and gives Carcetti the platform his S4 mayoral run is built on.

cliffhanger.text: The Barksdale organization is gone — Stringer dead in a half-built condo, Avon back in prison. Marlo Stanfield is left standing on empty corners, and Hamsterdam is a scandal the whole city just watched fail.
questions: Can Marlo take Baltimore without anyone left to stop him?
Does Carcetti's Hamsterdam speech actually get him City Hall?
Is there any way back for Colvin after being forced out in disgrace?

characters.name: Marlo Stanfield
characters.line: A cold young dealer with a habit of killing witnesses; refused Stringer's co-op and now stands to inherit the streets uncontested.

characters.name: Tommy Carcetti
characters.line: A white councilman who spent the season courting a run against Mayor Royce and now has Hamsterdam as his opening scandal.

characters.name: Bunny Colvin
characters.line: The Western District major who invented Hamsterdam, publicly disgraced when the press found out and pushed out of the department.

characters.name: Jimmy McNulty
characters.line: The homicide detective who chased Stringer for years; with Stringer dead he asks off the detail and starts seeing Beadie Russell.

characters.name: Cedric Daniels
characters.line: The detail's commander, promoted into Colvin's old major's job, now openly together with prosecutor Rhonda Pearlman.

characters.name: Roland Pryzbylewski (Prez)
characters.line: The detail's tech-savvy cop who just shot a Black plainclothes officer he mistook for a shooter; his police career is over.

characters.name: Dennis 'Cutty' Wise
characters.line: A Barksdale enforcer paroled after fourteen years who walked away from the game and opened a boxing gym for local kids.

characters.name: Omar Little
characters.line: The shotgun-toting stick-up artist who set Stringer up to be killed with Brother Mouzone after Stringer broke the Sunday truce trying to shoot him.

characters.name: Bubbles
characters.line: The detail's veteran drug-addict informant, last seen alone with Colvin in the wreckage of Hamsterdam.

beats.label: S4 · Bodies in vacants
beats.text: Marlo Stanfield's enforcers Chris and Snoop kill a rival dealer and seal him inside a boarded-up rowhouse — the method that will hide every body Marlo wants gone.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the vacants MO that becomes the season's central case and the investigation carried into S5.

beats.label: S4 · Four boys
beats.text: Prez, now a middle-school teacher, watches four kids drift toward the corner: Michael, Randy, Namond, Dukie. Namond's mother pushes him to deal; Michael refuses Marlo's money.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the four boys whose diverging fates are the season's spine and who must be recognisable in S5.

beats.label: S4 · Colvin's study
beats.text: Retired major Bunny Colvin joins a university study at the same school, sorting the corner-bound kids from the rest. He sees Namond as one he might still pull back.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up Colvin's bond with Namond and the season's argument about which kids the city can still save.

beats.label: S4 · Carcetti wins
beats.text: Scandals sink Mayor Royce, and Councilman Carcetti — a white politician in a Black city — takes the primary and the mayoralty, only to inherit a $54 million school deficit.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Carcetti as mayor and the budget hole he's inherited are the political engine of S5.

beats.label: S4 · Randy exposed
beats.text: Herc, chasing a bust of his own, lets Randy's name slip as a snitch. Marlo hears the boy talked, has his foster house firebombed, and Randy is sent to a group home.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Randy's ruin is the season's clearest verdict on the police, and the outcome the returning viewer will remember first.

beats.label: S4 · Michael turns
beats.text: Michael's abusive stepfather Devar returns from prison. With no one else to trust, Michael goes to Marlo; Chris beats Devar to death, binding Michael to Marlo for good.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Michael's move into Marlo's orbit produces the young soldier who is central to S5.

beats.label: S4 · Vacants opened
beats.text: Freamon opens the vacants and finds Marlo's dead. Bodie is killed after McNulty turns him, Sherrod dies on Bubbles's poison, Colvin adopts Namond, and Michael takes Bodie's corner.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The finale sets S5's opening board: Freamon's case, McNulty back on it, Bubbles at rock bottom, Michael on the corner.

cliffhanger.text: Freamon has opened the vacants and grasped the scale of Marlo's killing. Carcetti has just inherited the mayoralty, a $54 million school deficit, and the biggest homicide investigation the city has ever seen.
questions: Can Freamon build a case on Marlo before more bodies vanish?
Does Carcetti fund the vacants investigation, the schools, or neither?
What becomes of Michael, Dukie, and Randy now that their paths have split?

characters.name: Marlo Stanfield
characters.line: The rising drug boss whose crew hides its bodies sealed inside abandoned rowhouses; the police are only just catching on.

characters.name: Michael Lee
characters.line: Bright, guarded eighth-grader who went to Marlo for protection from his stepfather and is now Marlo's newest young soldier.

characters.name: Chris Partlow
characters.line: Marlo's chief enforcer; kills quietly with Snoop and buries the bodies in vacants.

characters.name: Tommy Carcetti
characters.line: New mayor of Baltimore, elected on reform, walking into office with a $54 million school deficit on his desk.

characters.name: Lester Freamon
characters.line: Now running major crimes; has just opened the vacants and grasped the scale of Marlo's murders.

characters.name: Jimmy McNulty
characters.line: Left the detail for Western patrol and a stable home life; returned to major crimes at season's end after turning Bodie.

characters.name: Bunny Colvin
characters.line: Retired major from the Hamsterdam year; ran a school study of corner-bound kids and, at season's end, took Namond home to raise.

characters.name: Namond Brice
characters.line: Wee-Bey's teenage son; pushed into the game by his mother, then rescued and adopted by Colvin.

characters.name: Randy Wagstaff
characters.line: Foster kid marked as a snitch by Marlo; his foster mother was badly burned when the house was firebombed and he was sent to a group home.

characters.name: Dukie Weems
characters.line: The other bright kid Prez tried to save; homeless, pushed up to a high school he can't handle, now working for Marlo.

characters.name: Bubbles
characters.line: Longtime informant whose young friend Sherrod died on heroin Bubbles had poisoned for someone else; now in rehab, guilt-crushed.
